Attention Creators, producer, hobbyist and composers. Are you bored, stuck, seeking inspiration or something new? Jam Maestro may be the app you have been looking for. I don’t know how many apps I have that are not user first focused and users either abandon or spend a frustrating amount of time scrolling and watching videos to learn about another app that has great potential and offers a unique experience. I absolutely adore this app!. Hello my name is Tommy, I wanted to start with how much I absolutely adore this app! It is by far my favorite music writing app for writing out tabs & midi for guitar and bass and have an amazing sounding demo track right out of my phone. I noticed a small bug where the 32nd not grid often doesn’t line up on the drum tracks along with the guitars and bass, as well as sometimes will not copy and paste the 32nd notes when copying sections, which really makes it difficult when composing and arranging. I think with a fix on the 16th/32nd/triplet note gridding it would really solve the inconsistency of the timing placement between tracks. Which would really help as I love using this app to write on the go without a computer, it just has a couple of limiting bugs that think hold it back from its full potential. As well it would be nice to be able to change time signatures throughout a song, as well as tempo. All in all an incredible app and I love to use it to write out ideas when they come up. I would love to see some of these fixes as I would love to use this app more and more for writing. Thank you for all that you do,
- Tommy

reviews.text: It’s amazing but it can be better. I honestly love this app, I’ve been using it to write all my drum tabs and it’s so easy to use. One of the best parts about this app is that I can have my Spotify premium going on in the background of the app and play my tab and the song at the same time to see if I missed anything or if I need to make some changes, I dont know if that was intentional on the creators part but they should never change it. A few things i would love to see added to this app is ghost notes and being able to write in between beats. You can already kind of write ghost notes in the app by just putting on a second drum set and lowering the volume, but you cant quite get the same affect, and so I would love to see that become a setting like how the guitars can mute and bend. Writing in between beats would be helpful just to use 12th notes to make beats more creative, it’s not the biggest deal not having it, I was able to write a tab to a song that used 12th notes by just spreading them out farther and closer to make it sound like it, but It would be appreciated to be able to do that without going through trial and error like I did. Besides those two features that I would really like to see added into any new update, I really love this app, I couldn’t recommend it enough to people who are looking to write their own covers, keep up the good work!

Lots to dig into and I’m still learning more cool stuff I can do with this app.
There are some hiccups here and there, but mostly with guitar fx. I did lose one session after clicking “Restore Session” when opening the app... could have been my error in saving, idk. I just cancel that every time I open the app and it works fine. 
Would love to see AU implementation! Definitely worth the money, especially on iPad. iPhone version is great also... just remember to turn the layout for different modes, that was confusing at first.
4/5 overall app

reviews.text:
Great replacement for Guitar Pro (IMO). Just got the app, so I’m still learning it, but this is so far the closest app I’ve ever found to get anywhere close to Guitar Pro 5, and Tab Maestro might actually be superior to it!

First off, it’s a guitar/bass/drum tab editor/composer, which means that if you are looking to write anything other than that (violin or orchestral sounds, for instance) you won’t find that here. That said, what it does, it does amazingly well! The app uses a horizontal/vertical flip design to alternate between tab editing and detailing the sound of the guitars or drums. You can set the guitar notes to palm mute or strum, you can set cymbal grabs, and the tonal choices and tuning options are so wide and varied, that anyone should be able to find what they are looking for to match their style. 

My two main complaints at this point are the aforementioned lack of other instruments, which might be asking too much from a tab editor centered on guitar tabs, and I have yet to successfully import a guitar pro tab file. The online FAQs state that Jam Maestro can open any gp3-5 file, but so far the app has only crashes each time I’ve attempted to load one. It’s possible I’m trying to open files that are too complex (Metallica’s Fade to Black, Enter Sandman and Orion) and the app just isn’t able to process it, or maybe I’m not opening them correctly. 

Regardless, those two complaints aren’t really something I expect others to share, as they are pretty specific. I imagine most users will really enjoy what this tab composer has to offer, especially if you’ve previously enjoyed The desktop Guitar Pro app and need a mobile alternative.

Thank you, to the creator of this app, and for reading my review. I hope it helps other like-minded musicians find what they are looking for.

I'm aware that gpx can be easily converted to gp5, but most tabs from UG for example are gpx, which means I cannot simply grab them using Safari and view them using only my iPad. Very powerful compositional tool. Jam Maestro is both easy to use and sounds great. The app is based around guitar tablature, which is likely familiar to most guitarists but easy to pick up if new. It comes with a variety of great sounding guitar, bass and drum samples. The instruments can be further tweaked with a nice set of apps, but the standard acoustic / metal / studio guitars sound great. Note entry is a breeze, with lots of little touches to facilitate the process, such as ability to insert 32nd notes where a quick run is required. The app also facilitates playing chords with a nice up / down strumming pattern.

It is easy to create an entire composition with rhythm, lead guitar, bass and drums that sounds great, and export it to a DAW for further work. I am using it know to work out an arrangement of a piece I have to play in my brother's wedding. I don't know the song well, but Jam Maestro is helping hear what different arrangement might sound like.

The developed is also very responsive. I've emailed him a few times since the app came out and he always responds quickly. He also updates the app regularly.

A must buy if you like to compose or create backing tracks on iOS!

reviews.text:
Great Features but would a couple more. First of all, I have tried lots of guitar apps over the years and Jam Maestro is the best I’ve tried so far. There are more features in this app than I know what to do with but learning g them slowly. However, I’ve been able to learn the basics very quickly and you can progress very quickly in writing tabs, quicker than other apps I’ve used.

The playback sounds are pretty good too for checking the accuracy of your tab. Velocity control would be nice.

Features I really appreciate:

Strum speed. This is so useful to have a more natural sounding strum and especially the ability to choose up or down strums. I wish the strum spacing was exported in the MIDI file though. 

Future strum features would be to have some preset or better, customisable strum patterns for rhythm guitar. And even better if this incorporated different string velocities to sound like a more natural strum. But... this is still the best feature I’ve seen on a guitar app like this.

I also love the ability to entire a whole chord at once and the range of chords is amazing. This really makes the process of writing tabs a much simpler process.

The ease at putting in slides, bends, hammer ons and pull offs is also fantastically easy and the quality of playback is good. Have t quite managed the vibrato yet which is a bit more complex but love the overall implementation.

The various export options are good too although I would like to see the ability to save to the iCloud Drive to make accessing files across devices easier. At the minute it is save to device or Dropbox. While Dropbox solves the problem, saving to iCloud Drive would so much quicker and easier. You can share via iTunes but sharing files via iTunes seems a bit old these days.

Overall this is a fantastic app and better than any I’ve tried before. 

Oh yeah. Just 2 more suggestions. 

1. On the tab, the ability to have tails/stalks to give an indication of timing of notes.

2. And have standard music notation alongside the tab. 

Toggle on and off for both of the above and be able to print both.

And one final suggestion. Triplets please 😀

Final comment, honest.

Great app, well worth the money in my opinion.

reviews.text:
Best guitar tab app. Best app I found so far for composing guitar tabs and hearing them played back to you. 

You can create multiple guitar parts, bass and percussion (I think you can even record your own live session, but I haven't tried that yet) and then playback to hear all the tracks simultaneously. 

Great samples with real attention to detail (like all the open strings and fretted notes are recorded individually so even notes that are technically the same vary in tonal quality to give a more realistic guitar sound). 

Nice range of guitar and drum samples (several acoustic styles, jazz, punk, rock, heavy metal etc. drums even include timpani (with beats/rolls/builds), tabla, conga, and snare/cymbal rolls). 

Once you get your head around the navigation it is a versatile music app.

3 features that I would love to see added are... Number 1. a capo option (you can adjust the tuning up/down but not beyond 3rd fret for top e string, so you can effectively play with a capo on 1-3rd frets but no higher, which is a bit frustrating) 

2. triplets would be super cool, particularly for the percussion.

3. being able to amplify or dampen/soften individual notes and phrases would be really nice as it can end up sounding a bit monotone and lacking modulation!

Quality App. Having used Tab software on the Pc, but not always having one in my back pocket I had longed for an app giving me the ability to throw some tabs down quickly and conveniently just when I needed. I even learnt a lot about different modes and scales from this app that I thought i had already understood.
I also have to praise the devloper who is constantly working on improving this app that he clearly loves and wants to improve to make it something he is proud of. He respond to all queries promptly and it always welcoming feedback, advice and ideas.
All in all it was an app I really wanted and was expecting a lot of but it came back with even more.
Polished and classy, intuitive but most of all fun and useful! Highly reccomended!

Every song in my band has been composed through this app. (a semi-complex metal band if that matters) it has the best sounding samples that ive heard from music apps, and you can modify them. Another side to the app is it helps with music theory because it gives you tons of scales. After you write a riff it can tell you what scale it is and it will give you notes so writing solos is really easy. It can change bpm and time signatures mid song, so its awesome for complex music. If youre a serious musician, this is the best app you can have. $10 is cheap considering what it can do
